given.part: An open loan's `dueOn` is before today (UTC)
given.why: Loans are lent on 03-02, so they are due 03-16, and the clock is set to 03-17 before the job runs.

given.part: it has no reminder recorded today
given.why: The test starts with no reminders, so both loans are eligible.

then.part: Asks the Notifications API to notify the loan's member
then.why: `sent` must hold each loan's own memberId, loanId and dueOn, and have exactly 2 entries.

then.part: then records a reminder for today
then.why: The reminders table must contain `{loan_id, sent_on: '2026-03-17'}` for each loan, and exactly 2 rows.

given.part: An open loan already has a reminder recorded today
given.why: The job runs twice, so the second run meets a loan that already has a reminder for today.
loan2 is overdue and is returned through the API before the job runs.
The third loan is lent on 03-03, so it is due exactly on 03-17, today. That is the boundary case.

then.why: `toMatchObject` on an array needs the same length, so `sent` must be exactly [loan1]. A repeat send, a send for the returned loan, or a send for the not-yet-overdue loan would fail it.

given.why: The fake refuses loan1 with a reason.
The fake only returns a refusal. An unreachable API is not set up here, but B5 shows it becomes a refusal.

then.why: The reminders table must hold only loan2's row.

then.part: logs `reminder.failed` at `warn` with `loanId` and the refusal's `error`
then.why: The log entry must match the level, event, loanId and error text exactly.

then.part: carries on with the other loans
then.why: The refused loan1 is lent first, and loan2 must still be sent afterwards.

given.part: The job has handled every overdue loan
given.why: Three overdue loans are set up, one of them refused, and the job runs through all of them.

then.why: The last log entry must equal info, reminders.finished and `{sent: 2, failed: 1}`.

given.why: The tests call the client directly with a reminder.

then.why: The captured request must have method POST and path /notifications.
The content-type header must be application/json, and the body is parsed as JSON.
The body is matched with `objectContaining` on memberId and data only. Nothing asserts the template, so a wrong template would pass.
`data` is compared as an exact object with loanId and dueOn.
202, 200 and 204 each have to give `accepted`, so a check for a single status would fail.

then.part: any other answer ... as refused, with a reason naming the status
then.why: A 400 must give `refused` with a reason containing '400'.

then.part: a failed connection as refused, with a reason saying the API was unreachable
then.why: A network error must give `refused` with a reason containing 'unreachable'.
